answer: Increasing gamma (walks per vertex) improves DeepWalk's classification performance, because more random walks give more training co-occurrence samples and better coverage of each vertex's neighborhood. The gains show diminishing returns, and most of the benefit appears at roughly gamma ≈ 10 walks per vertex, with further increases adding comparatively little.
confidence_reasoning: The direction of the effect (improvement with diminishing returns) is well supported, but I am not certain of the specific value (~10) that the paper's sensitivity analysis reports.
